description_full: Tenet Healthcare Corporation operates as a diversified healthcare services company in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Hospital Operations and Services, and Ambulatory Care. Its general hospitals offer acute care services, operating and recovery rooms, radiology and respiratory therapy services, clinical laboratories, and pharmacies. The company also provides intensive and critical care, and/or coronary care units; cardiovascular, digestive disease, neurosciences, musculoskeletal, and obstetrics services; outpatient services, including physical therapy; tertiary care services, such as cardiothoracic surgery, complex spinal surgery, neonatal intensive care, and neurosurgery services; pediatric quaternary care services through heart, liver, and kidney transplants programs; and limb salvaging vascular procedure, acute level 1 trauma, intravascular stroke care, minimally invasive cardiac valve replacement, imaging technology, surgical robotic, and telemedicine access services. In addition, it offers a range of procedures and services comprising orthopedics, total joint replacement, and spinal and other musculoskeletal procedures; gastroenterology; pain management; otolaryngology; ophthalmology; and urology. Further, the company operates acute care and specialty hospitals, off-campus emergency departments, imaging centers, urgent care centers, and micro-hospitals, as well as ambulatory surgery centers and surgical hospitals. Tenet Healthcare Corporation was founded in 1967 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas.

financial_summary: Tenet Healthcare Corporation is a large-cap healthcare business with a $22.5B market cap on $21.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +1% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 8% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $2.5B in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.52× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 16pp above the Healthcare median (0%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+4.3% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 458 companies in the universe; the top four hold 35% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 27% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 6% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 44% and a beta of 1.08, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.54 vs 5y 1.13), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $171.9M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 71% in the 2020 crash, 59% in the 2022 bear market and 87% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 75% below its DCF fair value of $1,153, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 52%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $726 to $1,827 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Healthcare peers: P/E 8.3 vs 25.5, EV/EBITDA 7.3 vs 15.7 and P/FCF 8.9 vs 23.7 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 288% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 11.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 22 covering analysts target $304 on average, 7% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 16% clears the cost of capital of 8.3% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.65).
It converts 12% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.52x.
ROE of 33% is amplified by 7.0x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 0.5% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.3x net debt to EBITDA ($2.9B of cash against $13.1B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 4.3x.
Goodwill makes up 38% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.6% over 3 years, 3.9% over 5 years and 0.6% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 16%).
At current returns, reinvesting 5% of profits supports about 0.9% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -2.5% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.2x, 4.7% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 15, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 29.2% on average.
own: Insiders hold little stock (1.0%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (24 sales, net $51.0M sold).
It returns 6.1% a year to shareholders (6.1% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 5.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 77,000 employees, each generates about $277K of revenue, 0.7x the Healthcare median, and productivity has risen 5.8% a year.
That works out to $33K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $11.4M (41x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
